newsitem.title: POLAND: Gec-Alsthom to up stake in Polish Konstal.
newsitem.headline: Gec-Alsthom to up stake in Polish Konstal.

text.p: French consortium Gec-Alsthom, which has 60 percent in Polish rolling stock producer Konstal SA, wants to up its stake in the firm to about 90 percent, the chairman of Konstal's supervisory board said on Thursday.

Hans-Juergen Jabs, representing Gec-Alsthom in Konstal's supervisory board, told a news conference, Konstal's share capital will be doubled in the next two weeks and all new shares will be taken by Gec-Alsthom.
He also said Gec-Alsthom offered to buy up shares held by employees, who have now 15 percent of the company.
"All the new shares will be taken by us and we think also employees will sell us some of their shares, so we think we will be close to 90 percent," he said.
Currently Konstal's share capital amounts to about three million zlotys.
Jabs said Gec-Alsthom had already invested four million zlotys in Konstal's technology and machinery and it was going to invest 11 million more this year.
Jabs also said further Gec-Alsthom's investments were possible in Poland but did not give any details.
"There is a desire to do more in Poland...I could imagine that we are going to look for other partners...but there are no detailed plans at the moment," he said.
Jabs declined to disclose not-yet-announced price of Konstal's 60-percent stake bought in Febuary from 15 Polish National Investment Funds.
"It's not the western practice to reveal the value of such transactions...the price is very high, in fact it's too high, but we wanted to be in Poland," he said.
Currently the state treasury holds a 25 percent stake in Konstal and employees have 15 percent.
Konstal, which employs 670, had sales of 29 million zlotys last year, but no profit or loss data was yet available. In the first half of 1996 it had a loss of 3.2 million zlotys.
